To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rock deformation is associated with the emission of mineral particles.
the emission of submicron mineral particles upon rock deformation is observed in experiments on the compression of rock samples.

(1) The particle emission is a function of the stress intensity factor, (2) the particle emission is independent of the rock strength, and (3) the particle emission increases with the increase of the particle size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emission of submicron mineral particles from rocks during their deformation, which is of great interest for understanding the processes of the destruction of rocks in nature.
the study of the emission of submicron mineral particles upon the uniaxially compressed rock samples and the development of the corresponding experimental technique.
the study of microparticle emissions upon rock deformation and the development of methods of their registration.

the particle emission is caused by the stress concentration and that the emission is a result of a complex interaction of several mechanisms.

the emission of particles upon rock deformation is caused by the processes of the formation and growth of microcracks in the vicinity of the hole and the formation of a stress field with a singularity.
